RESEARCH

Research areas

We synthesize nanoporous materials and put them to use. Sol–gel and hydrothermal routes give aerogels, porous metal oxides and metal catalysts, which we apply to water electrolysis, ammonia oxidation, CO₂ capture and energy storage. Synthesis conditions and measurements are kept as data, and machine-learning models trained on that data choose the next composition.

OVERVIEW

AI-guided design and nanoporous materials synthesis feed three application areas: adsorption and separation, catalysis, and electrochemistry.

Interactive overview ↗
01

AI-guided materials designAI 기반 소재 설계

Synthesis condition, structure and performance data are accumulated in the lab, and models trained on them propose the next composition to make.

  • Screening of electrocatalyst surfaces with universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (UMA, MatterSim)
  • Microkinetic modelling and selectivity prediction based on the computational hydrogen electrode and NEB
  • Active learning for synthesis condition optimization
  • Literature data extraction with large language models and data-driven activity prediction
02

Nanoporous materials synthesis나노다공성 소재 합성

Aerogels and porous metal oxides, metals and metal sulfides are synthesized by sol–gel, hydrothermal and solvothermal routes, followed by supercritical or ambient-pressure drying.

  • Metal oxide, metal and metal sulfide aerogels (SnO₂, RuO₂, NiFe-based and others)
  • Silica and organic–inorganic hybrid aerogels with improved mechanical strength
  • Control of pore structure and surface area; characterization by BET, SEM/TEM, XRD and XPS
03

Adsorption & separation흡착 및 분리

Molecular capture and separation using the surfaces and pores of porous materials.

  • Electrochemical CO₂ capture and release on MnO₂ electrodes and the effect of electrolyte cations
  • Heavy-metal and organic pollutant removal with functionalized silica aerogels
  • Selective adsorption controlled by pore size and surface chemistry
04

Catalysis촉매

Electrocatalysts with reduced noble-metal content, applied to water electrolysis, ammonia oxidation and plasma electrochemistry.

  • HER and OER catalysts for water electrolysis: RuNi alloy aerogels, NiFeSn oxyhydroxides, Pt clusters on SnO₂ aerogels
  • Ammonia oxidation (AOR) catalysts for direct ammonia fuel cells and nitrogen removal
  • Plasma electrochemistry for methane partial oxidation and NOₓ reduction
05

Electrochemistry전기화학

Porous electrode materials for electrochemical energy conversion and storage devices.

  • Electrodes and catalyst supports for water electrolyzers
  • Hierarchically porous metal oxides and sulfides for supercapacitor electrodes
  • SnO₂–carbon composite aerogels for lithium-ion battery anodes
